title: Hobby PWM Servo vs. Serial Bus Servo
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim comparing a hobby PWM servo (MG995) with a serial bus servo (STS3215): command and readback, leader/follower teleoperation, and wiring. Explains why hobby PWM servos cannot replace the STS3215 servos in an SO-ARM100/101 robot arm.

educational.topic: Hobby PWM servos versus serial bus servos
learningObjectives: Explain why a hobby PWM servo cannot replace an STS3215 bus servo in a leader/follower robot arm
Compare what a PWM servo and a bus servo report back to the controller
Compare the wiring needed for PWM and serial bus servos as the number of joints grows
prerequisites: Knows that a servo turns to a commanded angle

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, observe, explain with side-by-side comparison
keyQuestions: What does the controller learn about the servo when the arm is pushed short of its goal?
What would a leader arm have to read from a PWM servo?
How many wires does a 12-joint leader/follower pair need with each servo type?
commonMisconceptions: A servo with an internal feedback loop must be able to report its position
More torque makes a hobby servo a suitable replacement
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the readback of each servo before changing the load
Explain in two sentences why six MG995 servos cannot drive an SO-ARM101

assumptions: Both servos drive the same arm against the same load so only the telemetry differs
limitations: Load, shortfall, and temperature are teaching values, not datasheet measurements
